es: Comprender la postura, la necesidad y la cesión posible de cada parte en una discusión entre compañeros.

teaching.en: Leo's position is clear: he wants to play music after ten.
teaching.es: La postura de Leo es clara: quiere poner música después de las diez.
teaching.explanationEs: La postura (position) es lo que alguien pide: I want… / I'd like…
segments: Leo's position is clear: he wants
teaching.audioText: Leo's position is clear: he wants to play music after ten.

teaching.en: His real need is different: he wants time to relax after work.
teaching.es: Su necesidad real es distinta: quiere tiempo para relajarse después del trabajo.
teaching.explanationEs: La necesidad (need) es la razón de fondo que explica la postura.
segments: His real need is different: he
wants time to relax after work.
teaching.audioText: His real need is different: he wants time to relax after work.

teaching.en: Mia is willing to give up her Friday evenings if Leo uses headphones.
teaching.es: Mia está dispuesta a renunciar a sus viernes por la tarde si Leo usa auriculares.
teaching.explanationEs: Be willing to + verbo base: lo que alguien puede ceder; give up = renunciar a.
segments: Mia is willing to give up her
Friday evenings if Leo uses headphones.
teaching.audioText: Mia is willing to give up her Friday evenings if Leo uses headphones.

teaching.en: Their argument was about noise, but the common ground is that both of them need sleep.
teaching.es: Su discusión fue por el ruido, pero el terreno común es que los dos necesitan dormir.
teaching.explanationEs: El common ground es lo que ambos quieren aunque sus posturas choquen.
segments: Their argument was about noise, but the common
ground is that both of them need sleep.
teaching.audioText: Their argument was about noise, but the common ground is that both of them need sleep.

teaching.en: Mia was upset because nobody asked for her opinion.
teaching.es: Mia estaba molesta porque nadie le pidió su opinión.
teaching.explanationEs: Upset describe el enfado o malestar que suele acompañar a una discusión.
teaching.audioText: Mia was upset because nobody asked for her opinion.

teaching.en: Instead of shouting, Leo explains his need calmly.
teaching.es: En lugar de gritar, Leo explica su necesidad con calma.
teaching.explanationEs: Instead of + -ing sustituye una acción por otra mejor.
teaching.audioText: Instead of shouting, Leo explains his need calmly.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿cuál es la postura de Carlos?

choices.text: He wants to study in the living room.
He wants Sara to use the library.
He wants to cook every evening at eight.

feedback.es: La postura es lo que Carlos pide: cocinar cada tarde a las ocho. Estudiar y la biblioteca son cosas de Sara.

hint.es: La postura es lo que pide Carlos con «wants to».

origin.text: Flat 4 has a problem with the kitchen. Carlos wants to cook every evening at eight because he works late. Sara studies in the living room and she needs quiet after seven. Carlos is willing to cook earlier at weekends. Sara is willing to use the library on weekdays.

prompt.es: Completa la postura de Carlos y la necesidad de Sara según el texto.

feedback.es: Carlos quiere cocinar (postura) y Sara necesita silencio para estudiar (necesidad).

hint.es: Busca «wants to» para Carlos y «needs» para Sara.

sentences: Carlos wants to ___ every evening at eight.
origin.text: Flat 4 has a problem with the kitchen. Carlos wants to cook every evening at eight because he works late. Sara studies in the living room and she needs quiet after seven. Carlos is willing to cook earlier at weekends. Sara is willing to use the library on weekdays.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué está dispuesta a hacer Sara?

choices.text: She is willing to use the library on weekdays.
She is willing to cook at eight.
She is willing to study at weekends.

feedback.es: Be willing to introduce lo que Sara puede ceder: estudiar en la biblioteca entre semana.

hint.es: Busca «is willing to» junto al nombre de Sara.

origin.text: Flat 4 has a problem with the kitchen. Carlos wants to cook every evening at eight because he works late. Sara studies in the living room and she needs quiet after seven. Carlos is willing to cook earlier at weekends. Sara is willing to use the library on weekdays.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la necesidad de Mia.

choices.text: More friends at the flat.
A quiet flat late at night.
A bigger room on Saturdays.

feedback.es: Mia acepta las visitas, pero necesita el piso en silencio después de medianoche: esa es su necesidad.

origin.audio: Leo wants to have friends over on Saturdays. Mia agrees, but she needs the flat quiet after midnight.

prompt.es: Clasifica cada frase: postura, necesidad o cesión.

pairs: I work at night, so I need to sleep in the morning.
I'm willing to pay a little more.

feedback.es: Lo que se pide es la postura, el motivo es la necesidad y lo que se ofrece dar es la cesión.

pairs: I work at night, so I need to sleep in the morning.
I'm willing to pay a little more.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Leo está dispuesto a usar auriculares.»

answer.text: Leo is willing to use headphones

feedback.es: Be willing va seguido de to + verbo base para expresar lo que se está dispuesto a hacer.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿en qué pueden ponerse de acuerdo Tom y Mia?

choices.text: Cutting the whole tree.
Moving the kitchen window.
Cutting only the low branches.

feedback.es: Los dos aceptan lo mismo: Tom solo corta las ramas bajas y Mia lo permite. Ahí está el punto de acuerdo posible.

origin.text: Tom and Mia live next to each other and disagree about a tree. Tom wants to cut it because it blocks the light in his kitchen. Mia wants to keep it because it gives shade and birds live there. Tom is willing to cut only the low branches, and Mia is willing to let him do that.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué está dispuesto a hacer Carlos.

choices.text: Go by bus on Fridays.
Give Sara a lift to work.
Sell the car.

feedback.es: Carlos cede los viernes: irá en autobús si Sara lo lleva el sábado. Sara solo necesita el coche para trabajar.

origin.audio: Carlos wants the car every Friday, but Sara needs it for work. He is willing to take the bus on Fridays if she gives him a lift on Saturday.

prompt.es: Completa qué necesita Tom y qué le da el árbol a Mia según el texto.

feedback.es: Tom necesita más luz en su cocina y Mia quiere el árbol porque da sombra: son los motivos de fondo de cada uno, no sus posturas.

sentences: Tom needs more ___ in his kitchen.
Mia wants to keep the tree because it gives ___.
origin.text: Tom and Mia live next to each other and disagree about a tree. Tom wants to cut it because it blocks the light in his kitchen. Mia wants to keep it because it gives shade and birds live there. Tom is willing to cut only the low branches, and Mia is willing to let him do that.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase de Tom expresa una necesidad y no una postura?

choices.text: I want the bigger room.
I need a quiet room to sleep well.
I'd like to change rooms.

feedback.es: Una necesidad explica el motivo (dormir bien). Querer la habitación grande o cambiar de habitación son posturas.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase muestra que alguien está dispuesto a ceder algo?

choices.text: I want the room for myself.
I need the room to study.
I'm willing to give up my Saturday mornings.

feedback.es: Be willing to + give up indica lo que alguien puede ceder. Las otras frases dicen qué quiere o qué necesita.

prompt.es: Completa: «En lugar de gritar, Leo explica su necesidad.»

feedback.es: Instead of + -ing sustituye una acción por otra.

origin.text: ___ of shouting, Leo explains his need.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que necesita Mia.

choices.text: A chance to tell her side.
A new room.
An apology from Leo.

feedback.es: Mia está molesta porque nadie la escuchó y solo necesita cinco minutos para explicar su versión.

origin.audio: Mia is upset because nobody listened to her. She only needs five minutes to explain her side.
